question.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})$ of two functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ is defined as

$$
W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}|={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}^{′}.
$$

In our case, we have ${y}_{1}(x)={e}^{x}$ and ${y}_{2}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =({e}^{x}){(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{′}-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x){({e}^{x})}^{′} \\  & =({e}^{x})(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)({e}^{x}) \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-{e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$
